newsitem.title: USA: Prosecution rests in penalty phase vs McVeigh. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Prosecution rests in penalty phase vs McVeigh. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]

text.p: Prosecutors rested their case Friday in the penalty phase of the trial of convicted Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, presenting the last of 38 witnesses to testify about the impact of the blast on their lives and loved ones.

The defence was scheduled to begin presenting its opening statement and witnesses after a recess. The jury is to decide whether McVeigh is executed or spends his life in prison for the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building that killed 168 people.
The last of the witnesses included Oklahoma City Police Officer Don Browning, a former Marine and Vietnam veteran who described his recurring nightmare since rescuing bombing victims.

In his dream, he said, he is crawling into the rubble. "I begin to feel the ground tremble beneath me. It turns into a growl, a monstrous growl. I turn and run. The kids are crying. I feel so very guilty I didn't get to them," he said.

The jurors also heard a heart-wrenching letter written by 9-year-old Clint Seidl, whose mother was killed in the bombing. "I still make my mom Mother's Day and Valentine cards like the other kids," he wrote.
The seven men and five women on the jury found McVeigh guilty Monday of 11 federal charges, including conspiracy and murder.
